content_voiceover: T C F three colon colon P B X one ALL, which older literature calls E two A colon colon P B X one, results from the translocation t one, nineteen, q two three, p thirteen, and it's a classic, well-established fusion that's been on boards for years. Historically, this subtype was associated with a poorer prognosis compared to standard risk ALL, and in some cohorts it carried an increased risk of C N S relapse, so clinicians developed a habit of treating it more aggressively, including extended pulses of vincristine and dexamethasone during maintenance therapy. But this slide highlights a more recent and practically important finding from the Chinese Children's Cancer Group protocol, C C C G ALL twenty fifteen, which found that extended vincristine and dexamethasone pulse therapy is not actually necessary for children with T C F three colon colon P B X one positive ALL. This is a meaningful shift, because with modern risk-adapted, M R D-guided therapy, this subtype no longer requires the extra treatment intensity it once did, meaning less toxicity exposure for patients without sacrificing outcomes. This is exactly the kind of practice-changing update that boards like to test.
keypoints: Historically linked to poorer prognosis and higher CNS relapse risk
CCCG-ALL-2015: extended vincristine/dexamethasone pulses are not necessary
Reflects a shift toward less treatment intensity with modern risk-adapted therapy
